ops.text: 5.5 Proprietary Rights. As between the Parties, the Company owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to (i) the Content, the Marks and all other materials furnished by the Company under this Agreement, and (ii) all customer, user, order and transaction data collected through or generated by the Site in connection with Deerskin Products (the "Company Data"). HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in and to the design, look and feel, and other materials and work product developed specifically for the Company or the Site under this Agreement (the "Deliverables"), excluding HDI's pre-existing and generally applicable software, systems, tools and know-how, which HDI retains and in respect of which HDI grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the same to the extent embedded in or reasonably necessary to use the Deliverables. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to HDI any right, title or interest in the Content, the Marks, the Company Data or any other Company intellectual property, and no joint ownership of any of the foregoing is created.

With no clause at all, the rule's preferred and fallback positions are both unmet and the Company's Content, Marks and Site data are left unprotected (and could be claimed by HDI as developer/host). We have inserted a Proprietary Rights section (5.5) confirming Company ownership of Content, Marks and Company Data, assignment of the Site Deliverables to the Company with HDI retaining its pre-existing platform and tools under a perpetual, royalty-free licence back to us, and expressly excluding any assignment of Company IP/data to HDI and any joint ownership. ops.text: 9A.1 By HDI. HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors and employees, from and against any third party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) any allegation that the Site, the services performed by HDI hereunder or any materials, software or technology provided by HDI (excluding the Content and Marks provided by the Company) infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right of a third party; (b) HDI's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Content, Confidential Information or user or customer data caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct. 9A.2 By the Company. The Company shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless HDI from and against any third party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of any allegation that the Content or Marks furnished by the Company and used by HDI in accordance with this Agreement infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right of a third party, or out of the Company's breach of applicable law. 9A.3 Procedure. The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim (provided that failure to do so shall relieve the indemnifying Party only to the extent it is materially prejudiced), shall permit the indemnifying Party to control the defense and settlement of the claim (provided that no settlement imposing any liability or obligation on, or requiring any admission by, the indemnified Party shall be made without its prior written consent), and shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense.

There is therefore no HDI indemnity for third-party IP infringement arising from the Site it develops and hosts, no indemnity for HDI's breach of law, data/Content security incidents, or gross negligence/willful misconduct — this is walk-away territory under the rule (no vendor IP indemnity at all). Proposed insertion of a new Section 9A adds HDI's indemnity with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and keeps our reciprocal indemnity narrow (only Content and Marks we supply, plus our own breach of law), consistent with the preferred position; usual IP exclusions and procure/modify/replace remedies remain available as a fallback.

quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
rationale: Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated, Company-payable early-termination amount: 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, triggered by any Company termination. Because our fees under Section 3.1 are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month, this formula routinely exceeds a year's fees, so it fails the fallback of an early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. We therefore add a lesser-of cap at 3 months' Section 3.1 fees and state that the Termination Payment is the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company on termination.

proposal.summary: Add a Customer convenience termination right on 90 days notice and cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees.

quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
rationale: Section 4.1 only lets either Party stop the automatic one-year renewal on ninety (90) days written notice, so HDI's convenience right is already confined to the end of a term on 90 days notice (fallback-compliant), but the Company has no mid-term convenience right. Section 4.2(a) then imposes an uncapped exit fee on any Company termination (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments), which can far exceed three months' Section 3.1 payments. The clause therefore fails the fallback on two material terms. We take the fallback: an express Customer (Company) convenience termination on ninety (90) days written notice, and a cap on the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 payments.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: express Customer convenience termination at 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 day band), an express cap on the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 payments, and HDI's convenience right already confined to blocking renewal at each anniversary on 90 days' notice. Preferred is not met (90 rather than 30 days' notice, no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and HDI retains a convenience right), but the locked target is fallback. Minimal: two concise insertions only — the missing Customer convenience right and a cap operator on the existing Termination Payment formula; the formula, payment schedule and term mechanics are untouched. Intent preserved: the alias bridge "the Company is the Customer" avoids an undefined term, and the cap sits over (does not delete or contradict) the Net Sales-based Termination Payment calculation. Note for the rationale, not a deviation: the cap references Section 3.1 payments made rather than "fees paid or payable", and no pro-rata refund of prepayments is secured.
